# Answer: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

The strongest concrete rival I found is **last eligible**: build the same guide
bbox, the same row-major monochrome 4-connected component list, apply the same
floored bbox-center eligibility test, but crop the **last** eligible component
instead of the first. It fits both canonical training demonstrations (2/2)
because each has no observable first-versus-last choice. The source-bound fit
record is `checks/question-rival.json`.

The final production generator emits this exact lawful counterexample with:

```python
generate(seed=371801, sample_index=0,
         difficulty="easy", texture="teaching", frame_style="corners")
```

I checked this three ways. The exact canonical Racket program produced the 3×4
first output; a separately materialized Racket program that changes only
`glyphs` to `(reverse glyphs)` produced the 2×2 last output; and independent
Python mirrors agreed with both. Their program SHA-256 values are
`64c31afc01e4cba3642c80911d3517940c6cf93e1fc69ecd983aa50a7db7d315` and `0c6c4f50b235eb9d9575a2f4509cce201cf082565a765844f223650c5dff8924`.
The witness regenerated byte-for-byte from final generator SHA-256 `c9985a30b4ea46dd497b57229a9c8ffa92e7f866c968afe55495a97a89874862`,
passed `self_check`, and was observed as `texture="teaching"`. Full protected
bridge evidence is in `checks/parametric/evidence.json`; the compact replay is
`checks/question-rival.json`.

So the answer to whether the proposed generator emits such cases is **yes**.
Moreover, its default compound teaching schedule uses such multi-eligible cases
to refute this rival in demonstrations, and the 300-lesson census found the
rival refuted under every tested production lesson and query rotation.
